title: Is This What We Want?
summary:
Is This What We Want? is an album by various artists released on 25 February 2025 through Virgin Music Group. It consists of ambient noise recorded in recording studios, protesting the use of unlicensed copyrighted work to train artificial intelligence.

In December 2024, the UK government announced a consultation on copyright and AI, outlining a preferred approach that would see the introduction of a data mining copyright exception with a rights reservation package for rights holders. In the months following the announcement, a number of prominent musicians warned of the threat it posed to musicians, including Paul McCartney and Elton John.

The standard version consists of 12 tracks, each uncredited. The tracks consist of ambient noise recorded in recording studios, and the track titles form the sentence "The British Government must not legalise music theft to benefit AI companies." The album suggests that original music will be silenced if AI companies exploit musicians' intellectual property. It was organised by the British composer Ed Newton-Rex, who had previously worked at Stable Diffusion's parent company, Stability AI.

The silent album is co-written by more than 1,000 musicians, including Kate Bush, Annie Lennox, Damon Albarn, Billy Ocean, Hans Zimmer, Tori Amos, Yusuf / Cat Stevens, Imogen Heap, Max Richter, and many more. The album is available on streaming platforms like Spotify, listed under "1,000 UK Artists."
